title: Memory leak when sending PIL.Image to st.image()
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I'm trying to make a Streamlit web app that shows video-like detection results by constantly sending image detections to the frame_display. I have no problem with object detection and annotation and the web app runs smoothly, but memory usage kept rising. No memory leak problems when I commented on the frame_display.image part.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import cv2
import supervision as sv
from collections import defaultdict, deque
from inference import InferencePipeline
from inference.core.interfaces.camera.entities import VideoFrame
import streamlit as st
from PIL import Image

frame_display = st.empty()
SOURCE_VIDEO_PATH = #your video path here

#my_custom_sink loops in every video frame
def my_custom_sink(predictions: dict, video_frame: VideoFrame):
    #The detection part has no problem

    #Saving annotated video frame then displaying it to Streamlit web app
    example_frame= #example: video_frame
    example_frame_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(example_frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    image_pil = Image.fromarray(example_frame_rgb)
    frame_display.image(image_pil, caption="Annotated Frame", use_column_width=True)

pipeline1 = InferencePipeline.init(
    model_id= "yolov8n-640",
    video_reference= SOURCE_VIDEO_PATH,
    on_prediction=my_custom_sink,
)

pipeline1.start()
pipeline1.join()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

No memory leak, previous detection images are not stored anymore

### Current Behavior

streamlit\elements\image.py stored all the detection images

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.36.0
- Python version: 3.11.4
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

I suspect this leak is not caused by Streamlit. I just implemented PIL solely with Streamlit and have no memory leak problems. Probably from the Roboflow's 'inference' library

Try running my code, which does not have Roboflow in it anywhere, and watch your memory usage rise indefinitely. You'll need a bunch of images for it to pull from.

I am not confident enough in my understanding of the code to contribute a patch, but from what I read, I think this could be fixed by the media file manager having references to each session and coordinates in the image metadata. Then, when an image at the same coordinates in a session is replaced, you remove its reference, and when there are no more references, you remove the image from the cache. This is the reverse direction from the session and coordinate metadata that is already kept.

Hey [USER] I believe the script you wrote would increase the memory. This is due to the while true loop is probably generating images and loading them into streamlit and being slightly different enough that we can't dedupe or detect clear.

Have you tried:

1. Loading and manipulating all the images at once with caching and then just leverage those images. Those should resolve avoid processing multiple times.
2. Try a fragment with the `run_every` (See our [docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.fragment) for more info)

Curious if that improves the memory footprint.

A fragment with run_every is working well, but the image rotation is part of a larger program that uses libraries requiring asyncio, and I'm having trouble getting that to play nice - the fragment doesn't run again until the asyncio loop stops. I was also hoping to load new images at randomized intervals.

I also have the same issue
I am facing a memory leak issue in my Streamlit app, which is designed for real-time inference using video streams received via RTSP. The app continuously processes video frames and displays detection results in real-time.

To verify the issue, I created a minimal reproducible example with similar logic. The code below simulates random frames being displayed in a loop while monitoring memory usage:
```python

   return memory_info.rss / 1024 / 1024  

st.button('restart')

vid = st.empty()

memory_text = st.empty()
frame_count = 0
```
